_september_note: The first three cards retain their June press-reported tier. The June 11 CoreWeave and July 23 Galaxy cards were added from issuer primary sources on September 16. _september_addendum: September 16 issuer and SEC review added June 8 Stingray Compute and June 9 APLD ComputeCo 3 primary-source notes. Both are nominal five-year, secured, amortizing project notes; issue price makes the Stingray coupon different from yield. The covered universe remains selected observed prints, not a complete Rule 144A/private placement tape. Convertible notes and the 30-month IREN GPU equipment financing were inspected separately and excluded from the straight-credit S1 spread comparison.
_september_signal_audit: September 16 follow-up added original Bloomberg-reported Prime and Pure failed Nordic bond attempts for S1b. Both cards use the July 21 Bloomberg Law report date because exact withdrawal dates are unverified; an earlier Prime date in the first September audit draft was corrected before final handoff. Pure's bank replacement is issuer-confirmed, but neither issuer confirmed the failed bond, so that source-tier limit remains explicit. QTS August 27 $3.9 billion completed notes are verified by transaction counsel and a holder's September 10 portfolio identifies the 6.625% coupon. Under the registered coupon-versus-five-year-Treasury S1 proxy, QTS supersedes the July 23 stale Galaxy card. QTS issue price/yield and exact pricing date are not public in reviewed primary records. These selected prints do not establish an exhaustive deal census or a sector-wide financing halt.
